full_details: Bells from first light, and the Tower guns at dawn. At Paul's Cross the Bishop of London, Fletcher, was preaching. You did not stop. Twelve pence at the tiltyard gate, and a place far down the barrier, behind other men. Ten pairs. My lord of Essex against my lord of Cumberland. The herald cried my lord of Southampton against Scudamore. You were a hundred yards off. The earl kept his seat, as far as you could tell. The Queen was a stillness behind glass. A speech went toward her window, and nobody near you heard a word. On the way home the talk was a hermit, a soldier, and a secretary, pleading with my lord's squire, and that the gallery liked it. George Peele went by with a roll of paper. You nodded like old soldiers. You did not give him the groat. At the corner of Bishopsgate Street there was a bonfire, and the steeples were going. Mistress Ansell let Alse out. She said that is how you light a fire, for something. You did not explain the day. Upstairs you wrote one line. Hard-handed men, a play for the Duke's wedding, afraid of the lion. The memo was that you were bid to see him unhorsed, and he was not, and he will not know.
one_sentence: You walked west on the Queen's day, paid twelve pence at the gate, and came home to a fire and one line on the tables.
title: The earl kept his seat
